paper.title: LC-Tsallis-INF: Generalized Best-of-Both-Worlds Linear Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial regime (linear contextual bandit with i.i.d. contexts)
unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context X_t; the per-round action set depends on the context
loss parameter theta_t chosen by nature based on the history F_{t-1}
the learner knows the feature map phi and can compute Sigma(p)^{-1} exactly (knows the context distribution)
the learner knows an exploration policy e* with z^T Sigma(e*)^{-1} z <= 1/lambda and the constant lambda
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: Nature decides $\theta_t$ based on $\mathcal{F}_{t-1}$. The decision-maker observes a context $X_t \in \mathcal{X}$, generated from a fixed distribution $\mathcal{G}$. ... We assume that $| \left\langle z, \theta \right\rangle| \le 1$ ... $|\ell_t( a, x )| \le 1$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic regime with a margin condition
unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context
finite context support with every context probability >= 1/L (Assumption 2.3)
margin condition P(Delta(X) <= h) <= (1/2)(h/Delta_*)^beta for h in [0, Delta_*]
the learner knows phi, can compute Sigma^{-1} exactly, knows an exploration policy e* with constant lambda, and knows L
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: Consider the stochastic regime with fixed regression coefficient $\theta_0 \in \Theta$ ... there exists a universal constant $\Delta_* > 0$ and $\beta \in (0, +\infty]$, such that for any $h\in\left[0, \Delta_*\right]$, it holds that $\mathbb{P}\left(\Delta(X_t) \leq h\right)\leq \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{h}{\Delta_*}\right)^\beta.$

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint
unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context
finite context support with every context probability >= 1/L (Assumption 2.3)
(Delta_*, C, T) self-bounding constraint with per-context gaps Delta_t(a|x) >= Delta_*
the learner knows phi, can compute Sigma^{-1} exactly, knows an exploration policy e* with constant lambda, and knows L
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: We say that the DGP is in a $(\Delta_*, C, T)$-adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint for some $\Delta_*, C > 0$ if the regret $R_T$ is lower bounded as $R_T \geq \mathbb{E}[\sum_t\sum_{a\neq \rho^*_T(X_t)}\Delta_t(a\mid X_t) \pi_t(a\mid X_t)] - C$, where ... $\Delta_t(a\mid x) \geq \Delta_*$ holds.

unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context (context support not required finite)
the learner knows phi, can compute Sigma^{-1} exactly, knows an exploration policy e* with constant lambda
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: We consider the same formulation in our main text. However, we do not assume the finiteness of contexts in a stochastic regime.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic regime with a margin condition (BoBW-RealFTRL)
unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context
margin condition with parameter beta and constant Delta_*
the learner knows phi, can compute Sigma^{-1} exactly, knows an exploration policy e* with constant lambda
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: Assume that the loss is generated under a stochastic regime with a margin condition (Definition~\ref{def:margin}).

settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint (BoBW-RealFTRL)
unmapped: K arms with arm-dependent features phi(a, X_t) in R^d induced by an i.i.d. context
(Delta_*, C, T) self-bounding constraint with per-context gaps >= Delta_*
the learner knows phi, can compute Sigma^{-1} exactly, knows an exploration policy e* with constant lambda
comparator is the best fixed policy mapping contexts to arms
settings.definition_quote: Assume that the loss is generated under a linear contextual adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint (Definition~\ref{def:bounding}).

algorithms.name: BoBW-RealFTRL (FTRL with Shannon entropy, arm-dependent features)

symbols.lambda_exp: constant of the exploration policy: z^T Sigma(e*)^{-1} z <= 1/lambda for all features z

conditions: Assumptions 2.1, 2.2, 2.4: |<z,theta>|<=1 and |loss|<=1; i.i.d. contexts, known feature map, Sigma^{-1}(p) exactly computable; exploration policy e* with constant lambda

source.label: thm:regret_bound2
source.quote: Consider the $1/2$-LC-Tsallis-INF. Assume that the loss is generated under an adversarial regime. Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{asm:contextual_dist} and \ref{asm:contextual_dist2}--\ref{asm:bounded_random} hold. Then, the regret satisfies \[R_T = O\left(\sqrt{d \sqrt{K} T} + \frac{1}{\lambda}\left(\sqrt{K} + \frac{\sqrt{\sqrt{K}T}}{\sqrt{d}} \right) \right).\]

results.notes: Regret defined as max over policies of expected regret; mapped to pseudo_regret. Learning rate does not depend on T, so anytime. gamma_t uses L even when Assumption 2.3 does not hold (paper's statement).

bound.expression: ((1 + beta_m)/(beta_m*Delta_star))**(beta_m/(2 + beta_m))*(L_ctx*d*sqrt(K)*log(T))**((1 + beta_m)/(2 + beta_m))*T**(1/(2 + beta_m)) + sqrt(K*L_ctx/lambda_exp) + sqrt(K)*L_ctx*log(T)/(lambda_exp*d)

symbols.L_ctx: constant L >= S with every context probability >= 1/L

conditions: margin condition P(Delta(X) <= h) <= (1/2)(h/Delta_*)^beta for h in [0, Delta_*]

source.label: thm:regret_upper_margin
source.quote: Consider the $1/2$-LC-Tsallis-INF. Assume that the loss is generated under a stochastic regime with a margin condition (Definition~\ref{def:margin}). Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asm:contextual_dist}--\ref{asm:bounded_random} hold. Then, the regret satisfies R_T = O(((1+beta)/(beta Delta_*))^{beta/(2+beta)} (L d sqrt(K) log T)^{(1+beta)/(2+beta)} T^{1/(2+beta)} + kappa)

results.notes: For beta = infinity reduces to O(L d sqrt(K) log(T)/Delta_*); for beta=1 gives T^{1/3} rate (paper remarks).

symbols.Delta_star: minimum per-context gap Delta_* in the self-bounding constraint
symbols.L_ctx: constant L >= S with every context probability >= 1/L

source.label: thm:regret_bound3
source.quote: Consider the $1/2$-LC-Tsallis-INF. Assume that the loss is generated under a linear contextual adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint (Definition~\ref{def:bounding}). Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asm:contextual_dist}--\ref{asm:bounded_random} hold. Then, \[ R_T = O\left(\frac{L d \sqrt{K}}{\Delta_*}\log(T) + \kappa + C \right)\] holds.

results.notes: C is the self-bounding constant (C_sb). kappa expanded from Theorem 4.3.

bound.regime: dL sqrt(K)/Delta_* (log(T Delta_*^2/(L^2 d sqrt(K))) + 1) <= C <= Delta_* T / L

symbols.Delta_star: minimum per-context gap Delta_* in the self-bounding constraint
symbols.L_ctx: constant L >= S with every context probability >= 1/L

source.label: thm:regret_bound3
source.quote: Moreover, for $\frac{dL\sqrt{K}}{\Delta_*}\left(\log\left(\frac{T \Delta^2_*}{L^2 d \sqrt{K} }\right) + 1\right) \leq C \leq \frac{\Delta_* T}{L} $, the regret satisfies \[ R_T = O\left(\sqrt{\frac{C L\sqrt{K}d }{\Delta_*}\log_+\left(\frac{\Delta_*T}{CL}\right)} + \kappa \right).\]

tuning: 1/eta_1 = sqrt((1/lambda + d) log T / log K), entropy-adaptive learning rate

source.quote: Consider the BoBW-RealFTRL. Assume that the loss is generated under an adversarial regime. Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asm:contextual_dist} and \ref{asm:contextual_dist2} hold. Then, the regret satisfies \[R_T = {O}\left(\log(KT)\sqrt{ \left(\frac{1}{ \lambda} + d\right)\log(T)T}\right).\]

results.notes: Algorithm from Kuroki et al./Kato & Ito re-analysed for arm-dependent features; bound newly derived here. Bounded losses (Assumption 2.1) used in proofs though not listed in this theorem.

bound.expression: ((1 + beta_m)/(beta_m*Delta_star))**(beta_m/(2 + beta_m))*(log(K*T)*sqrt((1/lambda_exp + d)*log(T)))**((1 + beta_m)/(2 + beta_m))*T**(1/(2 + beta_m))

conditions: margin condition P(Delta(X) <= h) <= (1/2)(h/Delta_*)^beta for h in [0, Delta_*]
tuning: 1/eta_1 = sqrt((1/lambda + d) log T / log K)

source.label: thm:ftrl_shanon_margin
source.quote: Consider the BoBW-RealFTRL. Assume that the loss is generated under a stochastic regime with a margin condition (Definition~\ref{def:margin}). ... Then, the regret satisfies \[R_T = O\left(\left(\frac{1 + \beta}{\beta\Delta_*}\right)^{\frac{\beta}{2+\beta}}\left(\log(KT)\sqrt{ {\left(\frac{1}{ \lambda} + d\right)\log(T)}}\right)^{\frac{1+\beta}{2+\beta}}T^{\frac{1}{2+\beta}}\right).\]

results.notes: Proof omitted in paper ('almost the same as Theorem 4.3'). Assumption reference range '2.4--2.1' is ambiguous about whether finite support is assumed; paper says BoBW-RealFTRL does not require Assumption 2.3.

tuning: 1/eta_1 = sqrt((1/lambda + d) log T / log K)

source.label: cor:adversarial_regime
source.quote: Consider the BoBW-RealFTRL. Assume that the loss is generated under a linear contextual adversarial regime with a self-bounding constraint (Definition~\ref{def:bounding}). ... Then, the regret satisfies \[R_T = O\left(\frac{\left(\frac{1}{ \lambda} + d\right)\log(T)\log(KT)}{\Delta_{*}} + \sqrt{\frac{C\left(\frac{1}{ \lambda} + d\right)\log(T)\log(KT)}{\Delta_{*}}}\right).\]

results.notes: Arm-dependent feature re-analysis of FTRL with Shannon entropy.
